```{python}
#| label: setup
import json, pathlib
import pandas as pd
R = json.loads(pathlib.Path("../manuscript/analysis/results.json").read_text())
KM = R["roles_final"]["K"]
WORD = {4: "four", 5: "five"}
ROLE = json.loads(pathlib.Path("../manuscript/analysis/" + ("role_names.json" if KM == 5 else f"role_names_K{KM}.json")).read_text())
rid = {v: k for k, v in ROLE.items()}
A, V, L, I = R["paper_a"], R["paper_b_values"], R[f"lineup_model_roles_final_K{KM}"], R["ilp_validation"]
DC = I["dogrudan_eslestirilmis_fark"]
CV = V["RAPM_kosullu"]["PIR40"]; IV = V["olcum_hatasi_denetimi"]; RA = V["rol_duzeltilmis_kontrol"]
REF = ROLE["1"].lower()
T, S, C = L["test_R2"], I["amac_fonksiyonu_egimi"], I["ilp_beslisi"]
CD, OV = I["ilp_antrenore_gore_fark"], I["antrenor_beslisiyle_ortak_oyuncu"]
n = lambda x: f"{x:,}"
f2 = lambda x: f"{x:.2f}"
pp = lambda x: f"{100 * x:.2f}"
pc0 = lambda x: f"{100 * x:.0f}" if x >= 0.05 else f"{100 * x:.1f}"
ci = lambda v: f"{v[0]:.2f} to {v[1]:.2f}"
cipp = lambda v: f"{100 * v[0]:.2f} to {100 * v[1]:.2f}"
def slope(k): return f"{S[k]['egim']:.2f} (95% CI {ci(S[k]['GA95'])})"
def contrast(k): return f"{C[k]['fark']:.2f} (95% CI {ci(C[k]['GA95'])})"
```

# Abstract {.unnumbered}

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(f"**Purpose:** Box-score indices such as the EuroLeague Performance Index Rating (PIR) are widely used to value players, and decision-support frameworks optimise lineups on such values. We tested whether these indices depend on player role over and above on-court impact, whether they predict future lineup performance, and whether lineups optimised on them outperform coaches' own choices. "
f"**Methods:** Nine EuroLeague seasons ({n(A['games'])} games) were analysed. PIR and a related composite index (VAL) per 40 minutes were compared with regularised adjusted plus-minus (RAPM). Role dependence was quantified as the variance explained by {WORD[KM]} data-driven player roles, unconditionally and among players with the same RAPM. Predictive validity was assessed out of time (training 2016–2022, test 2023–2024) and within seasons (values from the first half, outcomes in the second half). Integer linear programming selected each team's highest-value five, which was compared directly with the five players given most first-half minutes. "
f"**Results:** Role explained {pc0(V['eta2']['PIR40'])}% of between-player variance in PIR but {pc0(V['eta2']['RAPM'])}% in RAPM. Among players with the same RAPM, role still explained {pc0(CV['kismi_eta2'])}% of the variance in PIR, and rim protectors and interior bigs were rated about {CV['rol_farki_RAPM_sabit'][rid['Rim protector']]:.1f} and {CV['rol_farki_RAPM_sabit'][rid['Interior big']]:.1f} PIR points per 40 minutes higher than {REF}s; the pattern persisted after correcting for measurement error in RAPM and with roles defined without PIR components. Out of time, RAPM explained {pp(T['RAPM'])}% of the variance in lineup net rating, compared with {pp(T['PIR40_toplami'])}% for PIR (difference {pp(T['RAPM'] - T['PIR40_toplami'])} percentage points, 95% CI {cipp(T['fark_GA95']['RAPM-PIR40'])}). Within seasons, RAPM-based lineup value and first-half minutes, but no box-score measure, had confidence intervals excluding zero. Adjusting PIR for role reduced the role effect at equal RAPM (partial η² {f2(RA['PIR40']['kismi_eta2'])} to {f2(RA['adj']['kismi_eta2'])}) but did not detectably improve prediction (out-of-time difference {pp(T['PIR40_rol_toplami'] - T['PIR40_toplami'])} percentage points, 95% CI {cipp(T['fark_GA95']['PIR40_rol-PIR40'])}). In direct within-team comparisons, optimised fives differed from the coach's most-used five by {min(v['fark'] for v in DC.values()):.1f} to {max(v['fark'] for v in DC.values()):+.1f} points per 100 possessions, with all 95% confidence intervals including zero. "
f"**Conclusions:** PIR-type indices rate interior roles higher than players with the same RAPM in other roles and should not be used to compare players across roles; adjusting them for role largely removes this bias but did not detectably improve their predictive validity. Lineup optimisation on these or on plus-minus values showed no evidence of an advantage over coaches' rotations, although differences of several points per 100 possessions in either direction could not be excluded; coaches' choices should be the benchmark for lineup decision tools.")
```

# Prior dissemination {.unnumbered}

The data source and part of the analytic approach were first used in the author's doctoral thesis (Ege University, Türkiye), which is available through the national thesis repository; the thesis's role-clustering and lineup-optimisation results are re-examined, and in part corrected, here: the thesis's seven player archetypes were not reproducible under resampling, and its lineup-optimisation approach did not outperform coaches' rotations out of sample. The full thesis reference will be added before submission. A companion manuscript on the same data addresses a different question (the derivation and stability of functional player roles).

# Data and code availability {.unnumbered}

All data were retrieved by the author from the publicly accessible EuroLeague application programming interface (live.euroleague.net and api-live.euroleague.net) in November 2026, and all analyses were run by the author with the open-source code. Code reproducing every number, table and figure is available at https://github.com/koksalahmet85-svg/sports-science-paper-engine and will be archived with a persistent identifier before submission; the exact code version, random seed and package versions used are recorded in the results file (`provenance`).

# Use of artificial intelligence {.unnumbered}

A generative AI assistant (Claude, Anthropic) was used to assist with literature search, programming and language editing. All numerical results were produced by deterministic, version-controlled code; all sources, analyses and interpretations were verified by the author, who takes full responsibility for the content.
